sources.excerpt: New Pedal: Land Devices Moonbow Filter + Overdrive | Delicious Audio Creative Pedals Creative Delay Tape Delay W/ Reverb Delay Distortion Fuzz Overdrive Dual Gain Dirt Boost Compr. + Dynamics Dynamics EQ Filter Wah Filter+EQ Lo-Fi 8 Bit Lo-fi Chorus Flanger Phaser Tremolo Uni-Vibe Modulation Pitch Shifter Octaver pitch Multiverb Reverb Spring Reverb Reverb CV In Granular Synth Pedals Synth Effect Guides Monthly Lists Shopping Guides Coverage Schedule Facebook Stompbox Exhibit New Pedal: Land Devices Moonbow Filter + Overdrive Updated Feb. 10, 2025  |  by Paolo De Gregorio Filter pedals, when followed by saturation or distortion, can become extremely effective “tone sculptors.” That’s precisely what the Land Devices Moonbow does, opening up a lot of sonic possibilities by elegantly placing an overdrive after a classic voltage-controlled dual-mode filter. The filter is a classic synth-style one, offering both High Pass and Low pass , with selectable Cutoff and Resonance for both modes. It operates on frequencies between 20Hz and 5kHz, and the manufacturer invites to acution when turning the resonance above 70%, due to strong oscillating tendencies. Tthe gain and level controls allow input flexibility, allowing compatibility with both level and line level instruments, but also the introduction of saturated tones, which can create edgy sounds by adding harmonics to the filtered tone. About • Collections • Blog • Compare • Privacy Policy • Terms of Service • Submit a pedal • © 2026 PedalFilter Clear Compare ( 0 ) Back Home Land Devices Moonbow Back to results Land Devices Moonbow Filter Overdrive Dual resonant filter with switchable HP/LP modes paired with channel-strip overdrive. Land Devices is a mysterious boutique pedal operation run out of Oakland, CA. Known for their minimalist aesthetic and refined takes on classic circuits, Land Devices has built a cult following among players seeking unique, well-crafted effects. The Moonbow combines a voltage-controlled resonant filter with a hot-rodded overdrive section derived from the Land Mixer's channel strip. The filter operates in either high-pass or low-pass mode via a toggle switch, with frequency sweepable from 20Hz to 5kHz. Resonance adds harmonic emphasis at the cutoff point, though settings above 70% can cause the filter to self-oscillate. The overdrive section offers gain ranging from -13dB to +20dB, working with both instrument and line level signals. A 3.5mm CV input on the front panel accepts external expression control, making the Moonbow ideal for integration with modular synths and expression pedals. The filter-into-drive topology creates everything from subtle harmonic enhancement to aggressive resonant saturation.
